investigation.Description: It is a procedure that enables the examiner (usually a Gastroenterologist) to examine your esophagus (swallowing tube), stomach, and duodenum (first portion of small bowel) using a thin flexible tube that can be looked through or seen on a TV monitor.

investigation.Name: ESOPHAGEAL MANOMETRY
investigation.Description:
Esophageal manometry is a procedure for determining how well the muscle of the esophagus works when diseases of the muscle are suspected.

When is esophageal manometry used?

Esophageal manometry is used primarily in three situations. The first is to evaluate the cause of reflux (regurgitation) of stomach acid and contents back into the esophagus (gastroesophageal reflux disease or GERD). The second is to determine the cause of problems with swallowing food. The third is when there is chest pain that may be coming from the esophagus.
At the start of the esophageal manometry procedure, one nostril is anesthetized with a numbing lubricant. A flexible plastic tube approximately one-eighth inch in diameter is then passed through the anesthetized nostril, down the back of the throat, and into the esophagus as the patient swallows. Once inside the esophagus, the tube allows the pressures generated by the esophageal muscle to be measured when the muscle is at rest and during swallows. The procedure takes 20 to 30 minutes.

investigation.Name: SIGMOIDOSCOPY
investigation.Description: Flexible sigmoidoscopy is a procedure enabling your doctor to examine the rectum and the lower colon. The instrument is a flexible tube 60 cm. long that is about the thickness of your finger and it is gently inserted into the anus and advanced slowly into the rectum and then the lower colon. It is an accurate and simple method for investigating rectal bleeding, change in bowel habits, rectal symptoms such as pain, diarrhea, etc. It is also a part of colon screening and surveillance for polyps and cancer prevention.

investigation.Name: MAMMOGRAM
investigation.Description:
A mammogram is an x-ray test that produces an image of the inner breast tissue on film. This technique, called mammography, is used to visualize normal and abnormal structures within the breasts. Mammography, therefore, can help in identifying cysts, calcifications, and tumors within the breast. It is currently the most effective way to detect early breast cancer. Breast self- examination (BSE) on a monthly basis and examination by a doctor are still important, but physical examinations typically find breast cancers when they are much larger than those detected by mammography. While mammography can discover a small cancer in a curable stage it not foolproof. Ten to fifteen percent of breast cancers are not identified by mammography and these cancers are found by physical examination. It is essential for a woman to perform monthly BSE and have a breast examination by her doctor in addition to the mammogram in order to most effectively screen for breast cancer. 
The American Cancer Society and the American College of Surgeons currently recommend that a woman obtain her first baseline mammogram between the ages of 35 to 40. Between the ages of 40 to 50 a mammogram should be done every other year. After the age of 50, a mammogram should be repeated yearly. Women who are at high risk for developing breast cancer may need to obtain mammograms earlier than these recommendations and at more frequent intervals.

investigation.Name: PCR
investigation.Description:
PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is a key technique in molecular genetics that permits the analysis of any short sequence of DNA (or RNA) without having to clone it. PCR is used to reproduce (amplify) selected sections of DNA. Previously, amplifying was done in bacteria, and took weeks. But now, with PCR done in test tubes, it takes only a few hours. PCR is highly efficient so that untold numbers of copies can be made of the DNA. What is more, PCR uses the same molecules that nature uses for copying DNA: 
Two "primers" that flag the beginning and end of the DNA stretch to be copied; 
An enzyme called polymerase that walks along the segment of DNA, reading its code and assembling a copy; and 
A pile of DNA building blocks that the polymerase needs to make that copy. 
Three major steps are involved in a PCR. These three steps are repeated for 30 or 40 cycles. The cycles are done on an automated cycler, which rapidly heats and cools the test tubes containing the reaction mixture. Each step -- denatauration (alteration of structure), annealing (joining), and extension -- takes place at a different temperature: 

Denaturation: At 94°C, the double-stranded DNA melts and opens into single-stranded DNA. 
Annealing: At 54°C, hydrogen bonds form and break between the single-stranded "primer" and the single-stranded "template." (The template provides the pattern to be copied.) The more stable bonds last longer and on that little length of double-stranded DNA (the joined primer and template), the polymerase attaches and starts copying the template. 
Extension: At 72°C, the polymerase works best. As a result, the attraction, created by the hydrogen bonds, of the primers to the template is stronger than the forces breaking these attractions. The upshot is that bases complementary to the template are coupled to the primer.
To do PCR, the original DNA that one wishes to copy need not be pure or abundant. It can be pure but it also can be a minute part of a mixture of materials. So, PCR has found widespread and innumerable uses -- to diagnose genetic diseases, do DNA fingerprinting, find bacteria and viruses, study human evolution, clone the DNA of an Egyptian mummy, etc.. Accordingly, PCR has become an essential tool for biologists, DNA forensics labs, and many other laboratories that study genetic material.
investigation.Remarks: PCR CAN BE DONE FOR ANY KIND OF INFECTIVE ORGANISM.

investigation.Name: PUS CULTURE TEST
investigation.Description:
CULTURE TEST HELPS IN ISOLATING THE OFFENDING AGENT AS WELL AS IN TREATING THE DISEASE BY FINDING OUT THE MOST SUITABLE DRUG AFTER SENSTIVITY TEST RESULTS.
THIS TEST CAN BE PERFORMED ON ANY BODY FLUID OR DISCHARGE TO KNOW THE OFFENDING AGENT & THE DRUGS TO WHICH IT IS SENSITIVE.

investigation.Name: CT NCCT WHOLE ABDOMEN
investigation.Description:
C.T. OR COMPUTERIZED TOMOGRAPHY IS UNIQUE BECAUSE IT CAN PRODUCE CROSS SECTIONAL IMAGES OF ANATOMIC STRUCTURES WITHOUT SUPERIMPOSING TISSUES ON EACH OTHER. ADDITIONALLY, CT CAN DISCERN THE DIFFERENT CHARACTERISTICS OF TISSUE STRUCTURES WITHIN SOLID ORGANS. AGENTS MAY BE USED FOR DELINEATION OF BLOOD VESSELS, THE OPACIFICATION OF CERTAIN TISSUE ( KIDNEYS ), DEMONSTRATION OF BOWEL, & BLOOD FLOW PATTERNS. THIS MEANS A CT SCAN CAN DEMONSTRATE MINOR DIFFERENCES IN DENSITY & COMPOSITION IN SHADES OF GREY. A CT SCAN CAN DIFFERENTIATE TUMORS FROM SOFT TISSUES, AIR SPACES FROM CSF & NORMAL BLOOD FROM CLOTTED BLOOD.
C.T. CAN BE PERFORMED ON ANY PART OF THE BODY LIKE : ABDOMEN, PELVIS, SPINE, HEAD, SINUSES, ORBITS, MASTOIDS, INTERNAL AUDITORY CANAL, FACIAL BONES, NECK, CHEST INCLUDING LUNGS, MEDIASTINUM & HEART, JOINTS & SPECIFIC BONES & CT GUIDED BIOPSY.CT CAN BE USED TO DETECT INTERVERTIBRAL DISC DISEASE, HERNIATION & SOFT TISSUE DAMAGE TO LIGAMENTS WITHIN JOINT SPACES.
IN C.T. LIGHTER THE SHADING, THE HIGHER THE DENSITY OF THE TISSUE OR STRUCTURE.

investigation.Name: PULMONARY FUNCTION TEST
investigation.Description:
THERE ARE THREE ASPECTS OF PULMONARY FUNCTIONS : PERFUSION, DIFFUSION & VENTILATION. PERFUSION RELATES TO BLOOD FLOW THROUGH PULMONARY VESSELS; DIFFUSION REFERS TO MOVEMENTS OF OXYGEN & CARBON DIOXIDE ACROSS ALVEOLAR CAPILLARY MEMBRANES; & VENTILATION RELATES TO AIR EXCHANGE BETWEEN ALVEOLAR SPACES & THE ATMOSPHERE.
PULMONARY FUNCTION TESTS DETERMINE THE PRESENCE, NATURE & EXTENT OF PULMONAY DISFUNCTION CAUSED BY OBSTRUCTION, RESTRICTION OR BOTH. PULMONARY FUNCTION STUDIES MAY REVEAL LOCATIONS OF ABNORMALITIES IN THE AIRWAYS, ALVEOLI & PULMONARY VASCULAR BED EARLY IN THE COURSE OF A DISEASE, WHEN THE PHYSICAL EXAMINATION & RADIOLOGICAL STUDIES STILL APEAR NORMAL.
INDICATIONS FOR THE TEST :
* EARLY DETECTION OF PULMONARY OR CARDIOGENIC PULMONARY DISEASE
* DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF DYSPNEA.
* PRESURGICAL ASSESSMENT.
* EVALUATION OF RISK FACTORS FOR OTHER DIAGNOSTIC PROCEDURES.
* DETECTION OF EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE.
* MONITORING PROGRESS OF BRONCHOPULMONARY DISEASE.
* PERIODIC EVALUATION OF WORKERS EXPOSED TO MATERIALS HARMFUL TO RESPIRATORY SYSTEM
* EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDIES
* MONITORING AFTER PHARMACOLOGICAL OR SURGICAL INTERVENTIONS.

investigation.Name: BRONCHO-ALVEOLAR LAVAGE FOR CYTOLOGY
investigation.Description: EXFOLIATED CELLS IN BODY TISSUES AND FLUIDS ARE STUDIED TO DETERMINE THE TYPES OF CELLS PRESENT & TO DIAGNOSE MALIGNANT & PREMALIGNANT CONDITIONS. THIS IS ESPECIALLY USEFUL IN DIAGNOSIS OF MALIGNANCY & IS NOW USED ROUTINELY IN THE CYTOLOGIC STUDY OF FEMALE GENITAL TRACT AS WELL AS IN MANY TYPES OF NONGYNAECOLOGICAL SPECIMENS.

investigation.Name: LIPIDS PROFILE
investigation.Description: IT IS ESTIMATION OF ALL DIFFERENT KINDS OF BODY FATS WHICH ARE IMPORTANT FOR CARDIO-VASCULAR OR CEREBRO-VASCULAR POINTS OF VIEW. TO SEE VALUES OR IMPORTANCE OF EACH ONE OF THEM GO TO THEIR INDIVIDUAL TEST RECORDS.

investigation.Name: CARDIAC DOPPLER
investigation.Description: TO SEE THE FUNCTIONING OF THE HEART, PRESSURE GRADIENTS , VALVULAR FUNCTIONS & OTHER ABNORMALITIES CARDIAC DOPPLER IS RECOMMENDED.

investigation.Name: MUCOSAL BIOPSY
investigation.Description: MUCOSAL BIOPSY LIKE ANY OTHER BIOPSY IS DONE TO KNOW THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF THE LOCAL DISEASE. THIS COULD BE FROM GUT, ESOPHAGUS RECTUM ANAL CANAL OR ANY OTHER MUCOSAL AREA.

investigation.Name: SERUM B12
investigation.Description: SERUM B12 LEVELS ARE AFFECTED IN MALABSORPTION CASES AS WELL AS IN DIETARY DEFICIENCY STATES LEADING TO MEGALOBLASTIC ANAEMIA.
investigation.Remarks: DECREASED : MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA DUE TO VIT B12 DEFICIENCY, PERNICIOUS ANEMIA, CHR. PANCREATITIS, BLIND LOOP SYNDROME, ILEAL DISEASE, ACHLORHYDRIA, BACTERIAL OVERGROWTH SYNDROME.

investigation.Name: SERUM CAROTENOIDS
investigation.Description: THERE ARE OVER 600 CAROTENOIDS INNATURE, & APPROXIMATELY 50 OF THESE CAN METABOLISED TO VIT A. BETA-CAROTENE IS THE MOST PREVALENT CAROTENOID IN THE FOOD SUPPLY THAT HAS PROVITAMIN A ACTIVITY. AFTER ABSORPTION CAROTENOIDS APPEAR IN THE SERUM WHICH CAN BE ESTIMATED NOW.
investigation.Remarks: DECREASED : MALABSORPTION SYNDROME, POOR DIETARY INTAKE OF VEGETABLES.

investigation.Name: SCHILLING TEST
investigation.Description: THIS TEST IS PERFORMED TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE FOR COBALAMIN MALABSORPTION. SINCE COBALAMINE ABSORPTION REQUIRES MULTIPLE STEPS, INCLUDING GASTRIC, PANCREATIC & ILEAL PROCESSES, IT CAN ALSO BE USED TO ASSESS THE INTEGRITY OF THESE OTHER ORGANS.THE TEST IS PERFORMED BY ADMINISTERING COBALT-58 LABELED COBALAMIN & COLLECTING URINE FOR 24 HRS & IS DEPENDENT UPON NORMAL RENAL & BLADDER FUNCTION.
investigation.Remarks: ABNORMAL ( < 10% EXCRETION IN 24 HRS ) - PERNICIOUS ANEMIA, CHR. PANCREATITIS, BLIND LOOP SYNDROME, ILEAL DISEASE

investigation.Name: URINARY D-XYLOSE TEST
investigation.Description: THE URINARY D-XYLOSE TEST FOR CARBOHYDRATE ABSORPTION PROVIDES AN ASSESSMENT OF PROXIMAL INTESTINAL MUCOSAL FUNCTION. D-XYLOSE, A PENTOSE IS ABSORBED ALMOST EXCLUSIVELY IN PROXIMAL SMALL INTESTINE. THIS IS USUALLY PERFORMED BY GIVING 25 GMS D-XYLOSE & COLLECTING URINE FOR 5 HRS. AN ABNORMAL TEST ( < 4.5 GM EXCRETION ) PRIMARILY REFLECTS THE PRESENCE OF DUODENAL/ JEJUNAL MUCOSAL DISEASE. THIS TEST CAN ALSO BE ABNORMAL IN PTS WITH BLIND LOOP SYNDROME & AS A FALSE POSITIVE STUDY, IN PTS WITH LARGE COLLECTION OF FLUID IN A THIRD SPACE LIKE ASCITIS, PLEURAL FLUID. THE EASE OF OBTAINING INTESTINAL MUCOSAL BIOPSY & THE FALSE NEGATIVE RATE OF D-XYLOSE TEST HAVE LED TO ITS DIMINISHED USE.
investigation.Remarks: ABNORMAL : MALABSORPTION SYNDROME DUE TO SMALL INTESTINAL PATHOLOGY

investigation.Name: STOOL FAT CONTENT 24 HRS
investigation.Description: IN MALABSORPTION FATS ARE NOT PROPERLY ABSORBED AND BY ESTIMATING 24 HRS STOOL FAT CONTENT WE CAN DIAGNOSE MALABSORPTION SITUATION. ON AN 80-100 GM/ DAY FAT DIET THE NORMAL FECAL FAT IS 2-6 GM / DAY
investigation.Remarks:
NORMAL - 0 - 6 GM / 24 HRS

INCREASED : PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY, CROHNS DISEASE, CHR PANCREATITIS, SPRUE

investigation.Name: COLONOSCOPY
investigation.Description: COLONOSCOPY IS DONE TO DIAGNOSE PATHOLOGY OF LARGE BOWEL LIKE SPACE OCCUPYING LESIONS INTUSSUSSEPTION, DIVERTICULAE, POLYPS ETC. A FIBRO-OPTIC COLONOSCOPE IS USED.

investigation.Name: SPUTUM FOR AFB STAINING
investigation.Description: IT IS DONE TO DIAGNOSE OPENNESS OF THE LUNG TUBERCULOSIS.

investigation.Name: SPUTUM FOR CULTURE & SENSTIVITY TEST
investigation.Description: THIS TEST IS DONE TO FIND OUT THE EFFECTIVE ANTIBIOTICS AGAINST THE OFFENDING ORGANISM.

investigation.Name: BRONCHOSCOPY
investigation.Description: BRONCHOSCOPY IS DONE FOR DIAGNOSING INTRALUMINAL GROWTHS BY EITHER TAKING BIOPSY OR BRONCHIAL SECRETIONS FOR CELL CYTOLOGY ETC.

investigation.Name: BRONCHOGRAPHY
investigation.Description: A RADIO-OPAQUE DYE IS USED FOR BRONCHOGRAPHY. THIS TEST IS DONE TO DIAGNOSE INTRALUMINAL PATHOLOGIES , BRONCHIACTESIS ATELECTESIS ETC.

investigation.Name: MRI
investigation.Description:
MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING IS A DIAGNOSTIC MODALITY THAT EMPLOYS ASUPERCONDUCTING MAGNET & RADIOFREQUENCY SIGNALS TO CAUSE HYDROGEN NUCLEI TO EMIT THEIR OWN SIGNALS TO CONSTRUCT DETAILED SECTIONAL IMAGES OF BODY. NO IONIZING RADIATION IS USED IN THIS. THE ABILITY OF MAGNETIC RESONANCE TO DISCERN ANATOMY IS MOST CLOSELY LINKED TO THE MOLECULAR NATURE OF TISSUE. SPECIAL TECHNIQUES PRIMARILY BASED ON THE MAGNETIC REACTIONS OF HYDROGEN NUCLEI CAN INFLUENCE THE MRI SIGNALS TO ENHANCE CERTAIN TYPES OF TISSUES ( FAT IS ACCENTUATED IN T-1 WEIGHTED IMAGES, CEREBROSPINAL FLUID & OTHEWR PURE FLUIDS ARE HIGHLIGHTED IN T-2 WEIGHTED IMAGES ). COMPUTER RECONSTRUCTION TECHNIQUES ALLOW IMAGES TO BE PRODUCED IN ANY PLANE AS WELL AS IN THE THREE DIMENTIONAL VIEWS.
INTRAVENOUS MR CONTRAST AGENTS, ALL PRIMARILY CONTAINING WATER SOLUBLE GADOLINIUM COMPLEX OR OTHER METALS SUCH AS MANGANESE & IRON ARE USED IN EVALUATING THE CNS . MR CONTRAST AGENTS HAVE LOWER TOXICITY & FEWER SIDE EFFECTS THAN X-RAY CONTRAST AGENTS. HOWEVER BECAUSE THESE AGENTS ARE PRIMARILY EXCRETED VIA KIDNEYS, RENAL FAILURE IS A CONTRAINDICATION FOR USE.

investigation.Description: BY TAKING BIOPSY OF THE DISEASED AREA WE CAN PIN POINT THE DEFINITE PATHOLOGY OR DIAGNOSIS OF THE DISEASE.

investigation.Name: HBSAG
investigation.Description: THIS TEST IS DONE TO DIAGNOSE THE PRESENCE OF HEPATITIS C-VIRUS IN THE BODY.

investigation.Name: GRAM STAINING
investigation.Description: GRAM STAINING IS DONE TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSATIVE ORGANISM IN THE SPECIMEN COLLECTED FROM THE LESION OR DISEASED AREA. THE BACTERIAS CAN BE GRAM POSITIVE OR GRAM NEGATIVE ETC, ETC.

investigation.Name: URINARY 5-HIAA
investigation.Description: 5-HIAA IS A METABOLITE OF SEROTONIN WHICH IS INCREASED IN CARCINOID SYNDROME. BOTH URINARY OR PLASMA SEROTONIN METABOLITS CAN BE MEASURED. THE TEST HAS 73% SENSTIVITY & 100% SPECIFICITY.
investigation.Remarks:
INCREASED : CARCINOID SYNDROME
FALSE POSITIVE : PATIENTS HAVING HIGH SEROTONIN FOODS LIKE BANANAS, PINEAPPLE, WALNUTS, PECANS, AVOCADOS, HICKORY NUTS OR TAKING CERTAIN MEDICATIONS LIKE COUGH SYRUPS CONTAINING GUAIPHENESIN, ACETAMINOPHEN, SALICYLATES, L-DOPA.

investigation.Name: MR ANGIOGRAPHY
investigation.Description: MR ANGIOGRAPHY IS NON INVASIVE HIGHLY SENSITIVE INVESTIGATION FOR DIAGNOSING ARTERIAL STENOSES, PLAQUES ETC.

investigation.Name: ELISA TEST
investigation.Description: ELISA TEST IS ENZYME LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAY & IS BASED ON ANTIGEN - ANTIBODY REACTIONS. THE COLOR CHANGE INDICATES ENZYME SUBSTRATE REACTION.

investigation.Name: BLOOD SUGAR ( RANDOM )
investigation.Description: GLUCOSE IS FORMED FROM CARBOHYDRATE DIGESTION & CONVERSION OF GLYCOGEN TO GLUCOSE BY THE LIVER. THE TWO HORMONES THAT DIRECTLY REGULATE BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVELS ARE GLUCAGON & INSULIN. GLUCAGON ACCELERATES GLYCOGEN BREAKDOWN IN THE LIVER & CAUSES THE BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVELS TO RISE. INSULIN INCREAES CELL MEMBRANE PERMEABILITY TO GLUCOSE, TRANSPORT GLUCOSE INTO CELLS, STIMULATES GLYCOGEN FORMATION, & REDUCE BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVELS.

investigation.Name: GASTRIC ACID ANALYSIS
investigation.Description: GASTRIC ACID ANALYSIS IS PERFORMED BY PLACING A NASOGASTRIC TUBE IN THE STOMACH & DRAWING SAMPLES AT 15 MTS INTERVAL FOR 1 HR. DURING UNSTIMULATED OR BASAL STATE ( BAQ) , FOLLOWED BY CONTINUED SAMPLING AFTER ADMINISTERING I.V. PENTAGASTRIN ( MAO )MAXIMAL ACID OUTPUT.
investigation.Remarks: UP TO 90% OF GASTRINOMA PATIENTS MAY HAVE A BAQ OF >=15 MEQ/H ( NORMAL <4 MEQ/H ). UP TO 12% OF PATIENTS WITH COMMON PEPTIC ULCER DISEASE MAY HAVE COMPARABLE LEVELS OF ACID SECRETION. A BAQ/MAO RATIO > 0.6 IS HIGHLY SUGGESTIVE OF ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME , BUT A RATIO <0.6 DOESNT EXCLUDE IT.

investigation.Name: MYOGLOBIN
investigation.Description:
MYOGLOBIN IS THE OXYGEN BINDING PROTEIN OF STRIATED MUSCLE. IT RESEMBLES HB BUT IS UNABLE TO RELEASE OXYGEN EXCEPT AT VERY LOW TWNSION. INJURY TO SKELETAL MUSCLE RESULTS IN RELEASE OF MYOGLOBIN. IT IS NOT SPECIFIC TO HEART MUSCLE. MYOGLOBIN IS NOT TIGHTLY BOUND TO PROTEIN & IS RAPIDLY EXCRETED IN THE URINE.
THE MYOGLOBIN TEST IS USED AS AN EARLY MARKER OF MUSCLE DAMAGE IN MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION & TO DETECT INJURY, DAMAGE OR NECROSIS TO SKELETAL MUSCLE. SERUM MYOGLOBIN IS FOUND EARLIER THAN CREATINE KINASE ENZYMES IN ACUTE MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION.
investigation.Remarks:
INCREASED : MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION( ELEVATES IN 1-3 HRS AFTER PAIN) , ANGINA WITHOUT INFARCTION, MUSCLE INJURY , POLYMYOSITIS , PROGRESSIVE MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY, MYOSITIS, RHABDOMYOLYSIS, INFLAMMATORY MYOPATHY ( SLE ) , TOXIN EXPOSURE ( NARCOTICS , MALAYAN SEA SNAKE TOXIN ), MALIGNANT HYPERTHERMIA , RENAL FAILURE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, TONIC CLONIC SEIZURES

DECREASED : CIRCULATING ANTIBODIES TO MYOGLOBIN ( MANY PATIENTS WITH POLYMYOSITIS ) , RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS, MYASTHENIA GRAVIS

investigation.Name: PLATELET COUNT
investigation.Description: PLATELET AGGREGATION IS USED TO EVALUATE FUNCTIONAL DISORDERS OF THE ADHESION, RELEASE OR AGGREGATION. IT IS RARELY USED TO EVALUATE ACQUIRED BLEEDING DISORDERS.
investigation.Remarks:
NORMAL : FULL PLATELET AGGREGATION IN RESPONSE TO THE FOLLOWING :
- ADENOSINE DIPHOSPHATE 
- COLLAGEN
- EPINEPHRINE
- THROMBIN
- RISTOCETIN

DECREASED RESPONSE IN CONGENITAL DISEASES :
- BERNARD-SOULIER SYNDROME , GLANZMANNS THROMBASTHENIA , STORAGE POOL DISEASES ( CHEDIAK- HIGASHI SYNDROME , GRAY PLATELET DISEASE ) , CYCLOOXYGENASE DEFICIENCY , WISKOTT-ALDRICH SYNDROME , ALBINISM , BETA- THALASSEMIA, MAY - HEGGLIN ANOMALY , VARIOUS CONNECTIVE TISSUE DISORDERS ( EG. MARFAN SYNDROME ) , VON WILLEBRANDS DISEASE

INCREASED AGGREGATION OCCURS IN PRIMARY & SECONDARY RAYNAUDS SYNDROME

DECREASED PLATELET AGGREGATION IN ACQUIRED DISEASES :
- UREMIA , ANTIPLATELET ANTIBODIES , CARDIOPULMONARY BYPASS , MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDERS , DYSPROTEINEMIAS (MACROGLOBULINEMIA) , IDIOPATHIC THROMBOCYTOPENIC PURPURA, POLYCYTHEMIA VERA , USE OF DRUGS & ASPIRIN, SOME ANTIBIOTICS , ANTI-INFLAMMATORY DRUGS, PSYCHOTROPIC DRUGS & OTHERS , DIC.

investigation.Name: D-XYLOSE ABSORPTION
investigation.Description:
THE D-XYLOSE TEST IS A DIAGNOSTIC MEASURE FOR EVALUATING MALABSORPTIVE CONDITIONS & INTESTINAL ABSORPTION OF D-XYLOSE, A PENTOSE NOT NORMALLY PRESENT IN THE BLOOD IN SIGNIOFICANT AMOUNTS. IT IS PASSIVELY ABSORBED IN THE PROXIMAL BOWEL, PASSES UNCHANGED IN THE LIVER, AND IS EXCRETED BY THE KIDNEYS.
THIS TEST DIRECTLY MEASURES INTESTINAL ABSORPTION. WHEN D-XYLOSE IS ADMINISTERED ORALLY, BLOOD & URINE LEVELS ARE CHECKED FOR ABSORPTION RATES.ABSORPTION IS NORMAL IN PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY BUT IS IMPAIRED IN INTESTINAL MALABSORPTION. IT IS A RELIABLE INDEX OF FUNCTIONAL INTEGRITY OF THE JEJUNUM IN PEDIATRIC PATIENTS.
investigation.Remarks:
NORMAL BLOOD LEVELS :
1- HR ABSORPTION OF 5 GM DOSE - INFANT: >15 MG / ML
1-HR ABSORPTION OF 5 GM DOSE- CHILD: > 20 MG / ML
2-HR ABSORPTION OF 5 GM DOSE- ADULT : >20 GM / ML 
2-HR ABSORPTION OF 25 GM DOSE- ADULT: > 25 GM / ML

URINE XYLOSE 5 HR REFERENCE RANGE FOR 25 G DOSE:
CHILD : 16% - 33% OF 5 GM DOSE
ADULT : > 16 % OF 5 GM 
ADULT 65 YRS OF AGE OR OLDER : > 14 % OF DOSE

URINE D-XYLOSE IS DECREASED IN :
INTESTINAL MALABSORPTION, IMPAIRED RENAL FUNCTION, SMALL BOWEL ISCHEMIA , WHIPPLES DISEASE, VIRAL GASTROENTERITIS , BACTERIAL OVERGROWTH IN SMALL INTESTINE.

D-XYLOSE TEST IS NORMAL IN :
MALABSORPTION DUE TO PANCREATIC INSUFFICIENCY , POSTGASTRECTOMY , MALNUTRITION.

investigation.Name: MYOCARDIAL PERFUSION TEST
investigation.Description:
TC-99 SESTAMIBI , THALLIUM-201 & TC-99 TETROFOSMIN ARE THE RADIOISOTOPES AVAILABLE FOR MYOCARDIAL PERFUSION IMAGING TO DIAGNOSE ISCHAEMIC HEART DISEASE & ALLOW DIFFERENTIATION OF ISCHAEMIA & INFARCTION. THIS TEST REVEALS MYOCARDIAL WALL DEFECTS & HEART PUMP PERFORMANCE DURING INCREASED OXYGEN DEMANDS. THESE SCANS MAY ALSO BE DONE BEFORE & AFTER STREPTOKINASE TREATMENT FOR CORONARY ARTRY THROMBOSIS, AFTER SURGERY FOR GREAT VESSELS TRANSLOCATION & AFTER TRANSPLANT TO DETECT ORGAN REJECTION & MYOCARDIAL VIABILITY. PEDIATRIC INDICATIONS INCLUDE EVALUATION FOR VSD & CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE & POSTSURGICAL EVALUATION OF CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE.
THALLIUM-201 IS A PHYSIOLOGIC ANALOGUE OF POTASSIUM. THE MYOCARDIAL CELLS EXTRACT POTASSIUM, AS DO OTHER MUSCLE CELLS. THE TC-99 IS TAKEN UPBY THE MYOCARDIUM THROUGH PASSIVE DIFFUSION, FOLLOWED BY ACTIVE UPTAKE WITHIN THE MITOCHONDRIA. UNLIKE THALLIUM, TECNETIUM DOES NOT UNDERGO SIGNIFICANT REDISTRIBUTION. THEREFORE, THERE ARE SOME PROCEDURAL DIFFERENCES. MYOCARDIAL ACTIVITY ALSO DEPENDS ON BLOOD FLOW . CONSEQUENTLY , WHEN THE PATIENT IS INJECTED DURING PEAK EXERCISE, THE NORMAL MYOCARDIUM HAS MUCH GREATER ACTIVITY THAN THE ABNORMAL MYOCARDIUM. COLD SPOTS INDICATE A DECREASE OR ABSENCE OF FLOW.
ADMINISTRATION OF DIPYRAMIDOLE OR ADENOSINE IS INDICATED IN ADULTS & CHILDREN WHO ARE UNABLE TO EXERCISE TO ACHIEVE THE DESIRED CARDIAC STRESS LEVELS & MAXIMUM CARDIAC VASODILATION. THIS MEDICATION HAS AN EFFECT SIMILAR TO THAT OF EXERCISE ON THE HEART. PHYSICAL STRESS TESTING MAY BE INITIATED IN CHILDREN BEGINING AT 4 - 5 YRS. CANDIDATES FOR DRUG INDUCED STRESS TESTING ARE THOSE WITH LUNG DISEASE , PERIPHERAL VASCULAR DISEASE WITH CLAUDICATION, AMPUTATION , SPINAL DISEASE OR INJURY, MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS OR MORBID OBESITY. DIPYRAMIDOLE STRESS TESTING IS ALSO VALUABLE AS A SIGNIFICANT PREDICTOR OF CARDIOVASCULAR DEATH , REINFARCTION & RISK FOR POSTOPERATIVE ISCHAEMIA & TO REVALUATE UNSTABLE ANGINA.

investigation.Name: MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION SCAN ( PYP )
investigation.Description: TC- 99 PYROPHOSPHATE IS THE RADIOACTIVE IMAGING AGENT USED TO DEMONSTRATE THE GENERAL LOCATION , SIZE & EXTENT OF MYOCARDIAL INFACTION 24 TO 96 HRS AFTER SUSPECTED INFARCTION & AS AN INDICATION OF MYOCARDIAL NECROSIS, TO DIFFERENTIATEBETWEEN OLD & NEW INFARCS. IN SOME INSTANCES THE TEST IS SENSITIVE ENOUGH TO DETECT AN INFARCTION 12 HRS TO 7 DAYS AFTER ITS OCCURRENCE. ACUTE INFARCTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH AN AREA OF INCREASED RADIO ACTIVITY ( HOT SPOT ) ON THE MYOCARDIAL IMAGE. THE TEST IS USEFUL WHEN ECG & ENZYME STUDIES ARE NOT DEFINITE.
investigation.Remarks: NORMAL DISTRIBUTION OF RADIO ACTIVE MATERIAL IN STERNUM , RIBS & OTHER BONE STRUCTURES . NO MYOCARDIAL UPTAKE.

investigation.Name: ARTERIAL BLOOD GASES TEST
investigation.Description:
Measurements of arterial blood gases ( ABGs ) are obtained to assess adequacy of oxygenation & ventilation, to evaluate acid-base status by measuring the respiratory & nonrespiratory  components, and to monitor effectiveness of therapy. They are also used to monitor critically ill patients, lo establish baseline values in the perioperative and postoperative period, to detect and treat electrolyte imbalances, to titrate appropriate oxygen flow rates, to qualify a patient for use of oxygen at home and in conjunction with pulmonary function testing. Reasons for using arterial rather than venous blood lo measure blood gases include the following:
1.   Arterial blood provides a better way to sample a mixture of blood from various parts of the body.
a.  Venous blood from an extremity gives information mostly about that extremity.  The metabolism in the extremity can differ from the metabolism in the body as a whole. This difference is accentuated in the following instances:
( I ) In shock states, when the extremity is cold or underperfused
(2) During local exercise of the extremity, as in opening and closing a list
(3) If the extremity is infected
b.  Blood from a central venous catheter usually is an incomplete mix of venous blood from various parts of the body. For a sample lo be completely mixed, the blood would have to be obtained from the right ventricle or pulmonary artery.
2.  Arterial blood measurements indicate how well the lungs are oxygenating blood.
a.  If it is known that the arterial 02 concentration is normal (indicating that the lungs are functioning normally) hut the mixed venous 02 concentration is low. it can he inferred that the heart and circulation are failing.
b.  Oxygen measurements of central venous catheter blood reveal tissue oxygenation hut do not separate contributions of the heart from those of the lungs. If central venous catheter blood has a low 02 concentration, it means either that the lungs have not oxygenated the arterial blood well or that the heart is not circulating the blood effectively. In the latter case, the body tissues must take on more than the normal amount of 0, from each cardiac cycle because the blood is flowing slowly and permits this lo occur: this produces a low venous 02 concentration.
3.  Arterial samples provide information about the ability of the lungs to regulate acid-base balance through retention or release of CO2. Effectiveness of the kidneys in maintaining appropriate bicarbonate levels also can be gauged. The radial artry is usually the site of choice
investigation.Remarks:
NORMAL VALUES FOR COMMON ARTERIAL BLOOD GASES

PHA - 7.35 - 7.45                            7.32 - 7.42
PACO2 - 35 - 45 MM HG                30 - 40 MM HG
PAO2    - > 80 MM HG                    80 - 100 MM HG
SAO2    - > 94 %
CO2 CONTENT - 45 - 51 VOL%
O2 CONTENT    - 15 - 22 VOL %
BASE EXCESS   - > 2 MEQ / L
BASE DEFICIT    - < -2 MEQ / L
HCO3                  - 22 - 26 MEQ / L

investigation.Name: HCV-RNA , QUANTITATIVE
investigation.Description:
THIS TEST CAN FIND GENETIC MATERIAL ( RNA ) UNIQUE TO THE HEPATITIS-C VIRUS. IT CAN BE DETECTED IN THE BLOOD 1-2 WEEKS AFTER EXPOSURE TO THE VIRUS. TWO TYPES OF HCV RNA TESTS ARE AVAILABLE :
* QUALITATIVE TEST
* QUANTITATIVE : THIS TEST IS DONE TO ESTIMATE THE NUMBER OF HCV PARTICLES IN THE BLOOD ( VIRAL LOAD ) & IT MAY PREDICT HOW LIKELY IS THE PATIENT TO RESPOND TO TREATMENT. DURING THE COARSE OF ANTIVIRAL DRUG TREATMENT, IF THE REPEAT TESTS SHOW DECREASING LEVELS OF HVC-RNA IN THE BLOOD, IT CONFIRMS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ONGOING TREATMENT. A HIGH LEVEL OF VIRAL LOAD IN THE BLOOD MAY MEAN LESS LIKELY HOOD TO RESPOND TO TREATMENT.
investigation.Remarks:
POSITIVE IN HEPATITIS C VIRUS DISEASE : HIGH VIRAL LOAD IS DEFINED AS > 2 MILLION COPIES OF THE VIRUS / ML

* FALSE NEGATIVE TEST RESULTS ARE ALSO POSIBLE.

investigation.Name: HCV-RNA , GENOTYPING
investigation.Description: THIS TEST IS USED MOST OFTEN TO DETERMINE WHETHER ONE HAS AN ACTIVE HEPATITIS-C DISEASE OR NOT. THIS IS IMPORTANT TO KNOW IF YOU ARE CONSIDERING TREATMENT FOR LONG-TERM( CHRONIC ) HEPATITIS C DISEASE. THE TEST ALSO MAY BE DONE TO CONFIRM A POSITIVE RESULT ON AN HCV ANTIBODY TEST ( SUCH AS ENZYME IMMUNOASSAY OR EIA ).
investigation.Remarks:
* POSITIVE IN HEPATITIS-C DISEASE

* IN RARE CASES ANTIBODIES AGAINST HEPATITIS-C VIRUS NEVER DEVELOP, SO TESTING FOR HCV ANTIBODIES CANT ALWAYS BE USED AS DIAGNOSTIC. IN THESE CASES, THE HCV-RNA TEST IS THE ONLY WAY TO TELL WHETHER YOU HAVE AN ACTIVE INFECTION.

investigation.Name: SERUM CALCITONIN ( THYROCALCITONIN )
investigation.Remarks: INCREASED : MEDULLARY CARCINOMA OF THYROID, C-CELL HYPERPLASIA, SMALL CELL CARCINOMA OF LUNG, NEWBORNS, PREGNANCY, CHR RENAL INSUFFICIENCY, ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME, PERNICIOUS ANEMIA

investigation.Name: SERUM BICARBONATE
investigation.Remarks:
INCREASED : COMPENSATION FOR RESPIRATORY ACIDOSIS( EMPHYSEMA ) & METABOLIC ALKALOSIS ( SEVERE VOMITING, PRIMARY ALDOSTERONISM, VOLUME CONTRACTION, BARTTER SYNDROME).

DECREASED : COMPENSATION FOR RESPIRATORY ALKALOSIS & METABOLIC ACIDOSIS ( STARVATION, DIABETIC KETOACIDOSIS, LACTIC ACIDOSIS, ALCOHOLIC KETOACIDOSIS, TOXINS LIKE METHANOL, ETHYLENE GLYCOL, PARALDEHYDE, THEN SEVERE DIARRHOEA, RENAL FAILURE, DRUGS LIKE SALICYLATES, ACETAZOLAMIDE, DEHYDRATION, ADRENAL INSUFFICIENCY.

investigation.Name: SESTAMIBI SCAN
investigation.Description:
Sestamibi Scan of the Parathyroid gland is a Nuclear Medicine procedure which is performed to identify hyperparathyroidism (or parathyroid adenoma). Sestamibi is a Nuclear Radiopharmaceutical which is bound to the radioactive isotope Tc99m. Tc99m-Sestamibi is taken up by both the thyroid gland and the parathyroid gland, and is also used in Nuclear Myocardial Perfusion Imaging. 
The general principal in the procedure is that the Tc99m-Sestamibi will absorb at a greater rate in a hyperfunctioning parathyroid gland than in a normal parathyroid gland. By using a Gamma Camera in Nuclear Medicine, the radiologist is able to determine if one of the four parathyroid glands is hyperfunctioning. The hyperfunctioning parathyroid gland will take up more of the Tc99m-Sestamibi, and will show up 'brighter' than the other glands on the gamma camera pictures. Sometimes this determination must be made three or four hours later when activity taken up by the thyroid gland fades away, while the parathyroid gland retains it's activity. 
                            By knowing which of the four parathyroid glands is hyperfunctioning, a surgeon is able to remove only the one parathyroid gland that is working too fast, and leave the other 3 glands in place. The remaining 3 glands are able to properly regulate the body even without the missing fourth gland.

investigation.Name: TB GOLD TEST
investigation.Description:
A REVOLUTIONARY TEST FOR DIAGNOSIS OF ACTIVE TUBERCULOSIS. CAN DETECT LATENT TUBERCULOSIS ALSO.THE TEST DETECTS INTERFERON GAMMA PRODUCED BY SENSITIZED T4 CELLS. THE TEST USES ESAT-6 & CFP-10 ANTIGENS. HIGHLY SENSITIVE ( 90% ) & SPECIFIC ( 98% ). THE TEST IS UNAFFECTED BY BCG VACCINATION OR NON TUBERCULAR MYCOBACTERIUM INFECTION. SITE SPECIFIC SAMPLE IS NOT MANDATORY & IS BETTER ALTERNATIVE TO BLOOD PCR. SINGLE TEST IS CONCLUSIVE. 
IT IS IMPORTANT TO EVALUATE LATENT TUBERCULOSIS IN FOLLOWING CASES :
* IMMUNOCOMPROMISED INDIVIDUALS LIKE HIV POSITIVE, PATIENTS ON CHEMOTHERAPY, IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE MEDICINES, INCLUDING TNF-? ANTAGONISTS.
* INDIVIDUALS WITH RISK FACTORS FOR TB REACTIVATION LIKE PATIENTS WITH DIABETES, CHR RENAL FAILURE, RENAL DIALYSIS, SILICOSIS, MALNUTRITION.
* INJECTION DRUG USER
* ORGAN TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS ( BEFORE TRANSPLANT )
* EXPECTANT MTHERS WITH H/O THREATENED ABORTIONS
* STAFF MEMBERS OF TB SURVEILLANCE PROGRAMS, HEALTH CARE WORKERS.
investigation.Remarks: 0.35 OR ABOVE 0.35 IU/ML IS POSITIVE

investigation.Name: TB RNA DETECTION BY TMA METHOD
investigation.Description: TRANSCRIPTION MEDIATED AMPLIFICATION METHOD IS IMPROVED PCR, WHICH IS THE ONLY US-FDA APPROVED RNA DETECTION SYSTEM. TEST IS SPECIFIC FOR MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS & DETECTS LIVE BACILLI ONLY. IT IS HIGHLY SENSITIVE ( 93.3% ) & SPECIFIC ( 99.1% ).

investigation.Name: TB DNA DETECTION BY REAL TIME PCR
investigation.Description: TEST IS SPECIFIC FOR MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS. THERE IS NO POSSIBILITY OF FALSE POSITIVE RESULTS DUE TO CONTAMINATION. THE TECHNIQUE IS BASED ON HYBRIDIZATION OF AMPLIFIED NUCLEIC ACIDS WITH FLUORESCENT-LABELED PROBES SPANNING DNA REGIONS OF INTEREST AND MONITORED INSIDE THERMAL CYCLERS. THE FLUORESCENT SIGNAL INCREASES IN DIRECT PROPORTION TO THE AMOUNT OF AMPLIFIED PRODUCT IN THE REACTION TUBE. THE SENSITIVITY RANGE FROM 71 - 98% WITH SPECIFICITY CLOSE TO 100%. THE SENSITIVITY OF THE TEST IS AFFECTED BY THE IRREGULAR DISTRIBUTION OF BACILLI IN THE CLINICAL SAMPLES LOWERING INITIAL VOLUME OF DNA PRESENT. THE MAIN ADVANTAGE IS ITS SPEED IN GIVING RESULTS ( 1.5 2 HRS AFTER DNA EXTRACTION) & THE DECREASE IN THE RISK OF CONTAMINATION SINCE BOTH REACTION & DETECTION OCCURS IN A SINGLE TUBE.
investigation.Remarks: POSITIVE : M. TUBERCULOSIS

investigation.Name: AMLICOR MTB TEST
investigation.Description: THE TEST DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS & MYCOBACTERIUM SPECIES OTHER THAN TUBERCULOSIS. IT IS AN NUCLEIC ACID AMPLIFICATION TEST WHICH AMPLIFY TARGET NUCLEIC ACID REGIONS THAT UNIQUELY IDENTIFY M. TUBERCULOSIS COMPLEX. BECAUSE NUCLEIC ACID AMPLIFICATION ( NAA ) TESTS CAN BE DIRECTLY USED ON CLINICAL SPECIMENS LIKE SPUTUM THEY ARE ALSO CALLED AS DIRECT AMPLIFICATION TESTS. IT IS A DNA-BASED TEST THAT AMPLIFIES THE 16 S RNA GENE USING GENUS SPECIFIC PRIMERS WITH DETECTION IN A COLORIMETRIC REACTION.
investigation.Remarks: POSITIVE : M. TUBERCULOSIS

investigation.Name: MYCOBACTERIUM DETECTION BY RAPID CULTURE METHOD
investigation.Description:
VERSATRACK METHOD HAS PROVEN TRACK RECORD OF FASTER DETECTION COMPARED TO BACTEC & HAS CONTINUOUS MONITORING SYSTEM WHICH CHECKS GROWTH EVERY 10 MTS. THE METHOD USES MYCOBACTERIA GROWTH INDICATOR TUBE SYSTEM.
THERE ARE TWO METHODS USED FOR RAPID CULTURE

1. MYCOBACTERIA GROWTH INDICATOR TUBE METHOD
2. TK MEDIUM
MYCOBACTERIA GROWTH INDICATOR TUBE SYSTEM IS BASED ON A GLASS TUBE CONTAINING A MODIFIED MIDDLEBROOK 7H9 BROTH TOGATHER WITH A FLUORESCENCE QUENCHING-BASED OXYGEN SENSOR EMBEDDED AT THE BOTTOM OF THE TUBE. WHEN INOCULATED WITH M. TUBERCULOSIS, CONSUMPTION OF THE DISSOLVED OXYGEN PRODUCES FLUORESCENCE WHEN ILLUMINATED BY A UV LAMP. IT ALLOWS FOR THE GOOD GROWTH OF MOST OF MYCOBACTERIAL SPECIES.
RECENTLY MGIT SYSTEM HAS BEEN FULLY AUTOMATED WHICH IS A NON-RADIOMETRIC, NONINVASIVE WITH THE TUBES INCUBATED IN A COMPACT SYSTEM THAT READS THEM AUTOMATICALLY.

investigation.Name: ANTI-CYCLIC CITRULLINATED PEPTIDE ( ANTI-CCP )
investigation.Description: THESE CYCLIC SYNTHETIC PEPTIDES, NOT RELATED TO FILAGGRIN OR OTHER KNOWN PROTEINS, WHICH ARE SPECIALLY RECOGNISED BY AUTO ANTIBODIES IN THE SERA OF RHEUMATOID PATIENT. THESE ARE ANTI-CCP FOUND IN RELATION TO JOINT INVOLVEMENT WITH RADIOLOGICAL DAMAGE IN EARLY RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS. THE TEST IS SUPERIOR TO OTHER AVAILABLE TESTS.
investigation.Remarks:
NEGATIVE : < 25 UNITS/ML
WEAKLY POSITIVE - 25 - 50 UNITS/ML
POSITIVE -         >50 UNITS/ML

investigation.Name: T SPOT-TB TEST
investigation.Description: IT IS AN ELISA TEST ( BASED ON RD1 ANTIGENS ) WHICH USES PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS AND ENZYME LINKED IMMUNOSPOT TECHNOLOGY. IT IS MUCH MORE SENSITIVE TEST THAN TUBERCULIN SKIN TEST BUT CAN NOT EASILY DISTINGUISH BETWEEN LATENT INFECTION & ACTIVE DISEASE.
investigation.Remarks: POSITIVE IN ACTIVE & LATENT TUBERCULOSIS.

investigation.Name: DENGUE NS1 ANTIGEN
investigation.Description:
DENGUE NS1 ANTIGEN IS A NONSTRUCTURAL PROTEIN THAT IS PRODUCED IN ALL PATIENTS INFECTED BY THE DENGUE VIRUS. IT IS EXPRESSED ON THE SURFACE OF INFECTED CELLS AND SECRETED INTO THE BLOOD STREAM OF THE INDIVIDUAL. IT CERCULATED AT HIGH LEVELS IN THE PATIENTS EXPERIENCING PRIMARY AS WELL AS SECONDARY INFECTIONS DURING THE ENTIRE CLINICAL PAHSE OF INEFCTION & IN THE FIRST FEW DAYS OF CONVALESCENCE.
THE ANTIGEN IS DETECTABLE ON THE VERY FIRST DAY THAT SYMPTOMS APPEAR AND CAN BE DETECTED UNTIL DAY 9.

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_short: Eat Nutritious diet,Stay away from smoking and alcohol altogether.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Eat Nutritious diet,Stay away from smoking and alcohol altogether.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: पौष्टिक आहार लें, धूम्रपान और शराब से पूरी तरह दूर रहें।
निर्धारित अनुसार उचित दवा का उपयोग करें।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Drink at least 8–10 glasses of water daily unless restricted by your doctor.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: जब तक कि आपके डॉक्टर द्वारा प्रतिबंधित न किया गया हो, प्रतिदिन कम से कम 8-10 गिलास पानी पिएं।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Incorporate a mix of carbohydrates, proteins, and healthy fats in every meal.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: प्रत्येक भोजन में कार्बोहाइड्रेट, प्रोटीन और स्वस्थ वसा का मिश्रण शामिल करें।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Consume a variety of fresh fruits and vegetables daily to ensure adequate vitamins and minerals.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: पर्याप्त विटामिन और खनिज सुनिश्चित करने के लिए प्रतिदिन विभिन्न प्रकार के ताजे फल और सब्जियों का सेवन करें।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Eat smaller portions 5–6 times a day instead of three large meals to avoid overburdening the digestive system.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: पाचन तंत्र पर अधिक बोझ से बचने के लिए तीन बार अधिक भोजन करने के बजाय दिन में 5-6 बार छोटी मात्रा में भोजन करें।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Limit intake of sugary, salty, and fried foods. Avoid packaged snacks and beverages high in preservatives.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: मीठे, नमकीन और तले हुए खाद्य पदार्थों का सेवन सीमित करें। डिब्बाबंद स्नैक्स और ज़्यादा प्रिज़र्वेटिव वाले पेय पदार्थों से बचें।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: If you have specific conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or kidney issues, follow the dietary restrictions advised by your healthcare provider. For post-surgical recovery, include protein-rich foods like eggs, lentils, and dairy products to promote healing.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: यदि आपको मधुमेह, उच्च रक्तचाप या किडनी संबंधी समस्या जैसी कोई विशेष समस्या है, तो अपने स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदाता द्वारा बताए गए आहार प्रतिबंधों का पालन करें। सर्जरी के बाद ठीक होने के लिए, उपचार को बढ़ावा देने के लिए अंडे, दाल और डेयरी उत्पादों जैसे प्रोटीन युक्त खाद्य पदार्थों को शामिल करें।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Take any prescribed vitamins or supplements as directed by your doctor.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: अपने चिकित्सक द्वारा निर्देशित कोई भी निर्धारित विटामिन या पूरक लें।

ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc: Ensure all meals are freshly prepared and hygienically cooked. Avoid raw or undercooked foods to reduce the risk of infections.
ipd_discharge_master_food.food_desc_lang: सुनिश्चित करें कि सभी भोजन ताज़ा तैयार किए गए हों और स्वच्छतापूर्वक पकाए गए हों। संक्रमण के जोखिम को कम करने के लिए कच्चे या अधपके खाद्य पदार्थों से बचें।

lab_repo.Title: DENGUE
lab_repo.HTMLData:
TEST RESULT
Dengue Ns1 {DNS1}
Dengue IgM {DIGM}
Dengue IgG {DIGG}

Dengue viruses is a flavivirus found largely in areas of the tropic and sub-tropics. There are four distinct but antigeniclly related serotypes of dengue viruses, and transmission is by mosquito, principally Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus.

Primary infection with dengue virus results in a self-limitig disease characterized by mild to high fever lasting 3 to 7 days, sever headache with pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, rash and vomiting. Secondary infection is the more common from of the disease in many parts of Southeast Asia and South America; IgM antibodies are not detectable until 5-10 days in case of primary dengueinfection and until 4-5 days in secondary infection after the onset of illness. IgG appear after 14 days and persist for life in case primary infection and rise within 1-2 days after the onset of symptoms in secondary infection.

Primary dengue virus infection is characterized by elevatons in specific NS1 antigen levels 0 to 9 days after the onset of symptoms; this generally presists upto 15 days. Earler diagnosis of Dengue reduces risk of compliation such as DHF or DSS, especially in countries where dengue is endemic.

lab_repo.HTMLData:
Test Name Result Unit Bio.Ref. Interval  Method
*D-Dimer
QUATITATIVE		 {DIMER} mg/L 0.00-0.5 Turbidimetric Immunoassay

Comments:

  • The formation of D-Dimer requires three hemostatic stages: formation of clot, Factor XIII a cross linking and clot breakdown of Fibrin
  • Several studies have shown a correlation of Increased D-dimer levels with clinical conditions that relate to the formation of Fibrin, mirroring an in-vivo lysis of formed cross-linker Fibrin.
  • These conditions include Deep Venous Thrombosis , disseminated intra-vascular coagulation, pulmonary Embolism, postoperative states, malignancy, trauma and pre-eclampsia. Signs and symptoms of Deep Venous Thrombosis are non-specific and present in a myriad of non-thrombotic disorders.
  • Sample Collected in citrate vial.
  • Increased levels have high risk for venons thromboembolism (VTE).
  • Lipemia falsely decreases D-dimer levels (intralipid value>250 mg/dl).

 Comments:

  • Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) is a glycoprotein with two covalently bound subunits. The alpha subunit is similar to those of Luteinizing Hormone (LH),Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH), and Thyroid Stimulating hormone (TSH).
  • In pregnancy the levels of hCG increases exponentially for about 8 to 10 weeks after the last menstrual cycle.
  • Later in pregnancy about 12 weeks after conception, the concentration of hCG begins to fall as the placenta begins to produce steroid hormones. Other sourcesof elevated hCG values are ectopic pregnancy, threatened abortion, and recent termination of pregnancy.

opd_clinical_templates.template_text: Patient conscious, oriented, cooperative. Vitals stable. No pallor/icterus/cyanosis/clubbing/edema. CVS S1S2 normal, RS clear bilaterally, P/A soft non-tender, CNS NAD.
Temp mildly elevated, pulse regular, BP stable. Throat mild congestion, chest clear, no focal neurological deficit, no neck rigidity. Hydration fair.
Afebrile, hemodynamically stable. Mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding/rigidity, bowel sounds present. No hepatosplenomegaly.
Acid peptic disease / gastritis without alarm features.
Acute febrile illness, likely viral etiology; monitor for warning signs.
Provisional diagnosis: Viral fever. Differential: early bacterial infection if fever persists >72 hours.
Provisional diagnosis: Dyspepsia / gastritis. Differential: GERD, peptic ulcer disease.
Provisional diagnosis: Essential hypertension on follow-up; control status to be assessed with home BP chart.
Counseled regarding hydration, medication compliance, and red-flag symptoms. If persistent high fever, breathlessness, chest pain, altered sensorium, or repeated vomiting, report immediately.
Antibiotic use explained with dose, duration, and adherence importance. Do not self-stop medication early. Report adverse effects promptly.
Lifestyle counseling done: diet moderation, salt restriction, regular physical activity, sleep hygiene, and follow-up adherence.
Adequate oral fluids, light diet, tepid sponging if required, rest. Maintain temperature chart. Review if fever not improving in 2-3 days or if warning signs appear.
Avoid spicy/oily food, tea/coffee excess, tobacco, and alcohol. Small frequent meals. Early dinner and avoid lying down immediately after meals.
Continue prescribed medicines regularly. Monitor BP at home and maintain log. Low-salt diet, regular walk, stress reduction. Follow-up in 2-4 weeks with BP chart.
